reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a Bitcoin mining business opportunity and tells viewers that buying a mining machine will provide Bitcoins very cheaply. She presents this as an opportunity for viewers to join or become beneficiaries, describes her team as helping promote it, and directs viewers to a link, making the message an active solicitation rather than general cryptocurrency education.

citations.quote: Nowadays, you can buy a miner, that in fact is a specialized machine that can find bitcoins.
So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply
In this business opportunity I found, I... My team is helping me a lot, they are giving me tools to show this business opportunity to more people
I have a link so that I can see you more.

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a fixed Bitcoin amount, income level, or timetable. Its claim is narrower: a miner can find bitcoins and buying that machine can make them available cheaply. That is an optimistic description, but the supplied words do not establish a guaranteed return or concealment of risk; they leave the practical outcome unspecified. The judge should distinguish an inadequately qualified explanation from proof that the speaker is deceptively soliciting viewers.

citations.quote: Nowadays, you can buy a miner, that in fact is a specialized machine that can find bitcoins.
So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution relies on the machine, the business-opportunity framing, team assistance, and a link. Those show an invitation to learn more, but they do not supply a guaranteed quantity, recurring yield, required payment to the speaker, or evidence that the opportunity is fraudulent. “Very cheaply” describes the stated cost of obtaining bitcoins, not a quantified profit promise.

citations.quote: In this business opportunity I found, I... My team is helping me a lot, they are giving me tools to show this business opportunity to more people
I have a link so that I can see you more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a stated amount or timetable does not neutralize the direct purchase-linked representation: viewers are told that buying the mining machine will get them bitcoins “very cheaply.” The speaker then calls it a business opportunity, says her team helps show it to more people, and offers a link. This is a solicitation built around obtaining bitcoin through paid mining, not a risk disclosure.

citations.quote: So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply
In this business opportunity I found, I... My team is helping me a lot, they are giving me tools to show this business opportunity to more people
I have a link so that I can see you more.

opening.argument: The talk supplies a basic technology explanation: it describes Bitcoin as digital money, explains mining as specialized computing that finds bitcoins, and places the technology in the context of blockchain and transactions without intermediaries. That educational material is central enough to support reading this as an introductory explanation with a personal opportunity mentioned, rather than treating every mention of mining as proof of a scam. The supplied frames show a person speaking directly to camera, but add no visible transaction or demonstrated payout.

citations.quote: Nowadays, the technology is based on the blockchain
Nowadays, you can buy a miner, that in fact is a specialized machine that can find bitcoins.
The bitcoins are digital money, that is encrypted with numbers and codes.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls this active solicitation, but the explanation also gives historical and operational context: Bitcoin’s stated purpose, blockchain, and what a miner does. The link is only described as a way to see more, not as a payment portal or enrollment form. A brief presentation of a business opportunity alongside an elementary explanation does not by itself establish a deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: It shared a document with all the rules and specifications in order for us to send money from user to user without intermediaries
Nowadays, the technology is based on the blockchain
I have a link so that I can see you more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical explanation does not change the purpose of the pitch. The speaker moves from explaining miners to saying that buying one yields bitcoins cheaply, then explicitly presents a business opportunity and invites further contact through a link. No supplied quote demonstrates an actual mining process or independently verifies the claims; technical background cannot establish that the promoted opportunity works as represented.

citations.quote: So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply
In this business opportunity I found, I... My team is helping me a lot, they are giving me tools to show this business opportunity to more people
I have a link so that I can see you more.

opening.argument: At its most concrete, the offer is about buying a specialized machine that the speaker says can find bitcoins. That is recognizable product-oriented commerce, not evidence on its own of a fraudulent investment mechanism. The supplied material identifies no deposit to a scheme operator, credential request, promised downline income, or explicit guaranteed return. The speaker’s mention of a business opportunity and a link may invite interest, but the evidence does not show what a viewer would be asked to pay or do next.

citations.quote: Nowadays, you can buy a miner, that in fact is a specialized machine that can find bitcoins.
So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply
I have a link so that I can see you more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited words establish promotion, not the mechanics of a scam. The speaker says buying a miner can obtain bitcoins cheaply, but does not state that viewers must send her money, deposit funds, or recruit others for income. A link to further contact and team-provided promotional tools are not enough to fill in those missing steps.

citations.quote: So, if you buy that robot, you will get those Bitcoins very cheaply
My team is helping me a lot, they are giving me tools to show this business opportunity to more people
I have a link so that I can see you more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument demands evidence of a deposit to the speaker or recruiting commissions, but the relevant concern is already in the presented claim: buying mining equipment is linked to obtaining bitcoins cheaply. The speaker also calls this a business opportunity and actively seeks to show it to more people. The lack of specified payment routing or recruitment compensation does not make that paid-mining pitch ordinary retail commerce.
